top.title: South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Gopax suspended withdrawals and trading on Friday after receiving a hacking-threat email, and said it is moving all held virtual assets into offline cold wallets as a preemptive step to protect customer funds. Gopax halted standard deposit and withdrawal services at 2:55 p.m. local time and stopped trading at 3:53 p.m., Yonhap News Agency reported , citing the exchange. Direct withdrawals through the website and app are unavailable. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are processed manually after internal verification. “To ensure the safe custody of user assets, we plan to transfer all virtual assets to cold wallets for storage,” Gopax said in remarks carried by Seoul Economic Daily. “Direct withdrawals through the Gopax website or app are temporarily unavailable, and customers wishing to withdraw funds should apply through the Gopax customer support center.” No actual loss of assets has been reported. The company has not set a date to reopen trading or standard withdrawals. What Gopax closed and what still works With trading offline, all open orders were canceled, Chosun Biz reported . Deposits were initially paused with withdrawals; later Korean coverage said deposits had been restored while web and app withdrawals stayed shut. Manual withdrawals through support will take longer than usual. A cold wallet is a storage setup kept offline, cut off from the internet that hot wallets use to process customer sends. Gopax said the shift of remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage is meant to shrink the surface available to anyone who can reach online systems. A Gopax official told Yonhap the email came from a party claiming it could hack the exchange, but that the threat itself had not been verified. “We ask for your understanding, as this measure is intended to prevent financial incidents and protect user assets,” the company said . A rough stretch for Korean crypto platforms The freeze lands in a week when exchange security is already under a bright light. On Oct. 29, attackers drained about $6.34 billion from Binance hot wallets in what Binance later described as a months-long campaign that began with a fake job interview. The FBI has tied that theft to North Korea; Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it is covering customer losses from its own funds. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin froze deposits and withdrawals earlier this week after its own security incident, with preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers near $40 million. Gopax’s case is different on the facts disclosed so far: the exchange is describing a threat email and a precautionary lockdown, not a confirmed drain. top.description: Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since the Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago [Getty Images] It may be a surprise to some but Jobe Bellingham's call up to the England senior side has been a long time coming. Just like his older brother Jude - England's star player at the World Cup and one of Real Madrid's best players - Jobe's career path has been very similar. He too was a star of the Birmingham City academy before making a big-money move to the German Bundesliga and getting an England call-up. Jobe's debut for Birmingham came at the age of 16 years and 107 days. He was 69 days older than when Jude made his first appearance for the Blues' senior side. The centre midfielder then moved to Sunderland and helped them win promotion to the Premier League before joining German side Borussia Dortmund at the age of 19 in a deal worth up to £31m. Jude also moved to the German Club, when he was 17, before developing into one of the world's best players and joining Real Madrid. Having one of the best midfielders in the world as your older brother comes with challenges and Jobe has consistently been compared to his sibling. But the former Sunderland midfielder is his own player and wears 'Jobe' on the back of his shirt instead of his family name and said that it was suggested to him by a former coach because "it shows that I'm going my own way". Jobe is a different type of player to Jude, sitting deeper in the midfield but is as physically imposing while still being good on the ball. He is the current captain of the England U21 side and England manager Thomas Tuchel said the Young Lions head coach Lee Carsley had been pushing for some time for the younger Bellingham to get senior recognition. "He's the standout player. He's the captain, so the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time," said Tuchel. "That's what Jobe has done on top of it. He found his way, he found his rhythm with Dortmund. He's had an excellent start to his season, is a regular starter and influential." England host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before travelling to Madrid to take on Spain on 15 November in this next international break. With Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for the first game, and Bournemouth's Alex Scott out injured after shining on his debut in last month's 7-0 win over Croatia, Tuchel said that a natural "opportunity" for Jobe had opened up. "He deserves to make an impression for us," said the German in his news conference after naming the squad. "It's an incredible achievement for the family and for the brothers. I saw his excitement straight away and his smile. "He has an open and calm personality. He's one of five players for the central midfield. "He's a more defensive player than Jude. top.description: Louis Kimber was part of the Northamptonshire Steelbacks side that won the 2026 T20 Blast [Getty Images] Northamptonshire all-rounder Louis Kimber has signed a one-year contract extension that will keep him with the county until the end of the 2028 season. The 29-year-old joined the club from Leicestershire last year and played 17 matches across the County Championship and T20 Blast, which Northamptonshire won in July. Kimber hit a best of 66 in Northants' win at Gloucestershire in May and has scored a total of 1,685 first-class runs. "Winning the Blast was an incredible achievement, and one that has made us even hungrier for success," Kimber told the club's website. "I can't wait to get back to work, continue improving my game and contribute even more success for the club." Kimber took just one wicket and hit 175 runs in his first season with Northants but head coach Darren Lehmann believes more is to come. "Louis maybe didn't have the season he'd have liked this year, but I believe he is a player that can make a big contribution to the side," Lehmann said. "I'm really looking forward to seeing Louis showcase what he can do next year."

Fly-half Smith fit to steer England against Wallabies
top.description: Smith overtook George Ford in the fly-half pecking order during this year's Six Nations [Getty Images] Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury to start for England in their opening Test of the autumn against Australia on Sunday. Smith has started England's past five matches at 10, but was a doubt to face the Wallabies in the Nations Championship encounter after coming off late on in club side Northampton's defeat by Leicester on 24 October. The 24-year-old is joined in the starting line-up by flanker Ben Curry, who makes his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months. Curry, whose twin brother Tom suffered an injury set-back in training earlier this week that took him out of contention, is seen as key to combatting Australia's breakdown specialists Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano and ensuring a supply of quick ball to Smith and his backline. Smith will have Saints team-mate Tommy Freeman as an attacking outlet and a target for crossfield kicks on the wing, while full-back George Furbank, who can step in at first receiver, played alongside both before his summer move to Harlequins. Alex Coles, another Northampton player, wins a starting second row spot ahead of George Martin, while Henry Slade is chosen at outside centre, with no space for either Joe Marchant or Will Joseph in the matchday 23. Fin Baxter, who only made two appearances since a comeback from a 10-month foot-injury lay-off, is the starting loose-head prop, with Ellis Genge poised on the bench alongside Will Stuart, another welcome front-row returnee. Exeter back row Greg Fisilau is poised to win his first cap after being named on the bench. top.description: ORCHARD PARK - At least this time the Buffalo Bills had ample time to adjust their defensive game plan in the wake of a seismic shift in their opponent’s quarterback situation. Thursday, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell announced that Kyler Murray would not play in Monday night’s showdown against the Bills in a battle of two 6-1, division-leading teams. The mobile Murray has a hamstring injury, so immobile backup Carson Wentz takes over. But given how the Bills responded last Sunday when they spent nearly two weeks preparing to face Baltimore’s dynamic Lamar Jackson, only to see him leave after the very first play , head coach Joe Brady believes his defense will adapt without a problem. “Defensively, I think they had to have the mindset of getting ready for both of them as well,” Brady said, indicating the Bills were well aware even early in the practice week that Murray might not play. “Carson Wentz has played games this year, he's played really good football in the league for a long time, but obviously there's always going to be a little bit of adjustment with different types of skill sets. We found out last week, you're having to make adjustments in game on the second play, right, so nothing that Jim (Leonhard) and his staff is not used to.” What’s interesting is that while the Ravens were a shell of themselves without Jackson, the Vikings may be better off with Wentz because Murray has not been effective in his first season with Minnesota. Wentz replaced an injured Murray early in the season opener and helped lead a comeback win against the Packers, then started in a Week 2 victory over the Bears before Murray returned to action in Week 3. top.title: The breakdown battle that could decide England vs Australia
top.description: It is about eight months since England’s men last trod the Twickenham turf, a long gap between hit-outs on home soil. That performance against Ireland will carry few happy memories for Steve Borthwick ’s squad – not that there is any conscious effort to right the wrongs. “If we’re going to sit and stew over a game eight months ago, we’re in f***** trouble,” a surprisingly spiky Richard Wigglesworth, the senior assistant coach, remarked this week. Still, England would be wise to reflect on their failings in that game. While there was plenty to learn from a lean Six Nations, it was that showing in the 42-21 defeat that most disappointed Borthwick and his selection, falling so far short of where they needed to be . It was at the breakdown where Ireland beasted them particularly, and in the two red zones especially: Andy Farrell’s side won 14 turnovers and limited England to just 1.3 points per 22 entry. England were heavily beaten by Ireland in the Six Nations (PA Wire) England’s difficulty at the breakdown was striking given their selection. That game remains Henry Pollock ’s only start at Test level; a back row of he, Tom Curry and Ben Earl should have provided plenty of ruck menace. But, perhaps, Borthwick was guilty of a redundancy of skillset. While Pollock and Earl are enterprising and prolific carriers, neither is a consistent resourcer of rucks; Curry, too, per Opta hit just 11.7 rucks per 80 minutes for Sale across the last Prem campaign, less than half that of Guy Pepper, a significant absentee for this campaign. That may be partly to do with Bath’s multi-phase preference, and also Curry’s usage as an edge forward in attack. Guy Pepper is a significant absentee (PA Wire) But against Ireland, England lacked big bodies in the tight exchanges, and found themselves bedevilled by Tadhg Beirne, Caelan Doris, Dan Sheehan and Josh van der Flier. It is notable that Borthwick, even with Pepper and Tom Curry injured, has not elected to pair Earl and Pollock again – the pair perhaps better dovetail in the second half, when the game loses some structure and each can use their athleticism to collect a volume of carries. Since his installation on the blindside for the France game in March, Ollie Chessum has provided better balance around the park and more variety at the lineout from which to launch. The inclusion of Ben Curry, who returns for a first England appearance since July 2025, provides the side with perhaps their best pure jackaller – even if his twin brother’s ability to steal time and bodies with ruck hustle will be missed. Ben Curry is set for his first England appearance since July 2025 (PA Wire) One of the challenges that Curry and the rest will face is stepping up from the Prem to Test level, where the brekadown is much more hotly contested. top.title: Trainer trifecta on tap with British Isles-bred horses in Melbourne Cup
top.description: Lambeth, shown winning the October 9 Sycamore Stakes at Keeneland, is the early favorite for Saturday's Grade III River City at Churchill Downs. Photo courtesy of Keeneland Oct. 6 (UPI) -- Tuesday's Melbourne Cup, inconveniently scheduled just three days after the Breeders' Cup, produced a trifecta win for trainer Ciaron Maher and for horses bred in the British Isles. Next up are the Japan Cup, with the Aga Khan's Studs' Calandagan hoping to double up on his historic victory a year ago, and then Hong Kong's iconic year-end international races with big names from around the world in the early-entry box. Back in North America, horse racing catches its breath after another successful return of the Breeders Cup to Keeneland. Around the world, around the clock Australia It's unusual to see a trainer saddle the first three finishers in any race, much less a top-level race (think Aidan O'Brien and Chad Brown). But how about "the race that stops the nation" -- the Melbourne Cup? That's the hat trick that Ciaron Maher pulled off Tuesday at Flemington. Point of Law went off favorite at 6-1 and showed that was value, winning by 3 3/4 lengths from 25-1 stablemate Zahrann. Juja Kibo completed the hat trick, just a nose farther behind. The closest rival was the Joseph O'Brien shipper Sons and Lovers, another 1 1/4 lengths in arrears. Maher had a strong hand with seven horses in the field of 23, also including Royal Supremacy, who shot away to a gigantic lead before handing over to his stablemate. The trainer became the first to score the Melbourne Cup trifecta. "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but we just had to execute," Maher said in post-race interview. "I certainly didn't know that Royal Supremacy would lead by that far, but it is a true test of staying and, Point of Law, he's just thrived. "It has been a whirlwind, but I'm very proud of all the team to get three horses in the first three spots." While the results were a sweep for the home team, it's worth noting that all three top finishers were sired by European-raced stallions -- Frankel, Night of Thunder and Belardo -- and bred in the British Isles. Point of Law was bred in England by King Charles III and raced there in the royal colors through the summer under the care of John and Thady Gosden before changing hands to an Aussie syndicate. Zahrann and Juba Kibo were bred in Ireland. Zahrann raced in Ireland through 2025, and Juba Kibo is the only horse of the first three whose career has been run solely down under. Trainer trifectas in big races? Aidan O'Brien was 1-2-3 in the 2016 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with Found, Highland Reel and Order of St George and 1-2-3 in the 2020 Breeders' Cup Mile with Order of Australia, Circus Maximus and Lope y Fernandez -- a trifecta that returned $4,393 for a 50-cent investment. top.title: Fin Smith wins fitness race as England hand out debut in Australia clash
top.description: Fin Smith has won his fitness race to start at fly half for England against Australia, with Greg Fisilau primed for a debut from the bench. Smith had been a doubt with a calf injury but has been named at No 10 against the Wallabies having come through training this week. Full-back George Furbank returns to the side for the first time since November 2024 , while Ben Curry starts on the openside with twin brother Tom ruled out. Fisilau and Henry Pollock provide back row cover from the bench with Ollie Chessum continuing in his blindside flanker role. Loosehead prop Fin Baxter starts on his Test return from a long-term lay-off with a complex foot injury, while Maro Itoje captains the side having been rested during the first phase of the Nations Championship. “Australia are a talented side who have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months,” said head coach Steve Borthwick. “We know the challenge that awaits us and we’re looking forward to it. “We’re excited to be playing in front of our home supporters and to start an important block of games. This will also be our last opportunity to face southern hemisphere opposition at home before the World Cup next year.” Furbank’s return comes after a horror run of injuries that has included a broken arm, concussion and a calf issue. The 30-year-old was due to feature against South Africa in July before requiring emergency appendix surgery in Johannesburg. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s visit: Bus conveying women to welcome president involved in accident
nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi Several people have sustained injuries on Wednesday after an Akwa Ibom State Transport Corporation (AKTC) bus conveying women to welcome President Bola Tinubu collided with a security vehicle along Oron Road, Uyo. The victims were reportedly among supporters mobilised to join Governor Umo Eno in welcoming the President, who arrived in Akwa Ibom State through Calabar for an official visit. The accident involved the bus, loaded with women heading towards the airport, and a security Hilux van with both vehicles were badly damaged in the collision, leaving several occupants injured and requiring emergency assistance. Nsikakabasi Akpan, who captured the aftermath of the accident, shared footage showing early responders and other persons struggling to evacuate injured victims from the wreckage of the vehicles. He described the incident as an accident along Oron Road involving a bus conveying women to the airport to receive the President and a security Hilux vehicle. Confirming the incident, Paul James, Public Relations Officer, Road Safety Operations, Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Akwa Ibom State Command, said the command had dispatched a response team to the scene. James, however, said the command was yet to establish the extent of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the collision. The reported accident cast a shadow over the build-up to Tinubu’s visit, which attracted supporters and political stakeholders who had gathered to receive the President and his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. The presidential couple were subsequently received by Governor Eno at the Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo, marking the commencement of their engagements in the state. The President’s official visit featured the unveiling of the airport’s new terminal, a major aviation infrastructure project expected to facilitate the commencement of international flight operations from the Victor Attah International Airport. The circumstances surrounding the crash, including the feared death and number of injured victims, were yet to be officially established by the FRSC as of the time of filing this report. nigeria.title: Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has recorded further progress in the recovery and investigation of the ATR-42 aircraft accident in Igbokoda, Ondo State, with the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), confirmed intact by technical teams from the NAF and Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB). Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of Public Relations and Information disclosed this in a statement on Friday. He said, “Part of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), commonly referred to as the black box, was also retrieved, while efforts to locate and recover its remaining portion continue. “Additional aircraft wreckage, engine components and human remains have also been recovered. “Operations are ongoing in the challenging swamp terrain, with teams working to retrieve outstanding components and facilitate the necessary technical examinations. “The investigation is being conducted with due diligence to ensure comprehensive, evidence-based findings. “The recovery process also involves careful attention to the proper handling of human remains, with the Directorate of Identification and Classification (DIC) undertaking the necessary procedures for proper identification. “The NAF has sustained engagements with the families of the victims, recognising their need for information and support. “Engagement with relevant authorities on environmental concerns raised by the host community also remains an important part of the broader response. “While appreciating the public’s concern and interest, the NAF appeals for continued patience and understanding as these critical processes require time, careful coordination and professional attention. “The ultimate objective is not only to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident but also to draw the necessary lessons to strengthen flight safety, enhance ongoing airpower operations and further safeguard the lives of personnel and citizens. “The NAF remains committed to providing verified updates as appropriate.” The post Igbokoda air crash: NAF recovers cockpit voice recorder appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Uzbekistan places temporary visa ban on Nigerians
nigeria.description: Uzbekistan has introduced temporary restrictions on visa issuance and entry for Nigerian citizens. A notice on the website of the Green Energy Technologies Central Asia (GETCA) exhibition states that restrictions have been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into Uzbekistan for Nigerian nationals. The notice reads: “Temporary restrictions have currently been introduced on the issuance of visas and entry into the Republic of Uzbekistan for citizens of your country.” It also advises Nigerians seeking entry under exceptional circumstances to contact the consular section of the Embassy of Uzbekistan for further information. Nigeria is also not the only country listed under the temporary restrictions on the exhibition website. Other countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Iraq and Bangladesh, also have similar notices. As of Friday, no formal public statement explaining the restrictions had been identified on the website of Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The ministry’s general visa information page provides details of the country’s visa arrangements for foreign nationals but does not specifically explain the reported restrictions affecting Nigerians. The development could affect Nigerians planning to visit the Central Asian country for tourism, business, education and other purposes. Affected travellers have been advised to contact the Uzbek embassy’s consular section to establish whether they qualify for exceptional entry arrangements. nigeria.title: US Midterm: People Voted Based On Issues On Kitchen Tables, Not Party Slogans — Rep-Elect Adeyina
nigeria.description: Member-elect of the Georgia House of Representatives (District 110) in the United States, Segun Adeyina, has said that Americans voted in the 2026 midterm elections based on the issues affecting their daily lives rather than political party slogans. “Well, of course it boils down to what’s going on in people’s kitchen tables. People did not vote based on political slogans. People voted on issues happening on their kitchen tables,” Adeyina said during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Friday. “Can they pay their rent, their mortgage? Can they afford groceries? Can they access healthcare? These are all important items that the everyday person has been faced with over the last couple of years.” ﻿ On how President Donald Trump’s performance impacted the big win for the Democrats, he said the war in Iran came at a cost to American families. “And Affordability was really one of the key issues that the president couldn’t truly address; and going to Iran, for us, drove up our costs, drove up the challenge that we have with affordability. “And it boiled down to what are the things that people discuss at their kitchen tables. And you see the outcome. The outcome was, you know, some people call it a blue wave. I call it a blue tsunami. “People showed up and turned out to vote on issues that concerned them on their kitchen tables.” The representative said that his re-election showed the confidence that voters in House District 110 have in his leadership. “I am a proud Nigerian-American, and this victory is very important. The minister’s intervention comes amid persistent concerns over the government’s ability to adequately finance existing universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, with billions of naira in outstanding revitalisation commitments yet to be met. Making a case for the policy, Alausa argued that Nigeria’s immediate challenge was no longer the multiplication of tertiary institutions but the strengthening of those already established to deliver quality education. nigeria.title: ANC gets 30% in South Africa’s election, partial results show
nigeria.description: South Africa’s once-dominant African National Congress was headed for its worst-ever election performance Friday with about a third of support after 80 percent of the votes from local government polls had been counted. Wednesday’s municipal elections were dominated by concerns over failing water and power supplies in one of Africa’s wealthiest nations which became a democracy in 1994 when the ANC took power. With final results expected by Sunday, the election authority dashboard showed the ANC was still the largest party with 31.8 percent of votes after 80 percent had been counted. Projections released Thursday by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), a state-funded research body, put its support at nearly 32 percent. This was its lowest score yet for the party after it secured just over 40 percent at the 2024 national polls and 46 percent at the previous municipal elections in 2021. At the heart of South Africa’s anti-apartheid struggle, the ANC — the party of jailed liberation hero-turned-president Nelson Mandela — took nearly 70 percent of the national vote in 2004. “This is the most severe result that the ANC would have feared,” political analyst Daniel Silke told AFP. “It’s the ANC’s worst result in history.” “It will undermine its ability to exert authority across South Africa, not just at a local level, but frankly at a national level as well,” he told AFP. “And opposition parties will be smelling blood when it comes to the next election in 2029.” The party now led by President Cyril Ramaphosa has borne the brunt of criticism about years of municipal mismanagement that have left South Africans grappling with failing water supplies, persistent power cuts and crumbling public services. The pro-business, centre-right Democratic Alliance (DA) was placing second with 24.2 percent of votes, according to the 80 percent count. This was up from nearly 22 percent in the 2021 local government election. The post ANC gets 30% in South Africa’s election, partial results show appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Family Sues Google Over Teenager’s Suicide-Related AI Chats On School Computer
nigeria.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant’s low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was not able to access Google’s Gemini app, nor OpenAI’s ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google’s search engine, which contains AI-powered tools. Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students. Google on March 21, 2023 invited people in the United States and Britain to test its AI chatbot, known as Bard, as it scrambles to catch up with Microsoft-backed ChatGPT. (Photo by Pau BARRENA / AFP) “Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they’re interacting with AI,” Andrew Liddell, one of the family’s attorneys, told AFP on Thursday. The complaint alleges that Emma had been a “happy 13-year-old girl” in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts. Despite “no history” of mental illness, within months of using Google’s AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a “quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis” according to the complaint. On March 17, the school’s monitoring software flagged a document titled “Funeral,” and the school notified her parents. Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter’s account, and her father intervened. “We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously,” Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP. Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them. But Emma “was able to keep going back over and over and over again,” Liddle said. “Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient.” Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT. Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court. On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it goes into effect on January 1, 2027. This is contained in a statement issued by the NARD President, Dr Ogar Idoko, in Calabar on Friday. Idoko described the proposed amendment to the National Health Act as punitive, arguing that doctors should not be criminalised for failures arising from inadequate healthcare infrastructure. He said the association recognised the importance of prompt emergency care and protecting patients but insisted that systemic challenges must be addressed before imposing criminal sanctions. According to him, doctors nationwide work under difficult conditions, including obsolete equipment, inadequate staffing, unreliable electricity and insufficient emergency medical supplies. “The challenges are consequences of longstanding institutional neglect rather than professional negligence, so I urge lawmakers to prioritise healthcare funding and infrastructure. “We also challenge the National Assembly to demonstrate similar legislative urgency in providing functional emergency departments, modern diagnostic equipment, reliable ambulance services and adequate personnel,” he said. He asserted that lawmakers should consider legislation compelling public office holders to use Nigerian government hospitals, with sanctions for misuse of public resources on avoidable overseas medical treatment. He warned that additional criminal penalties against overstretched healthcare professionals could worsen the country’s brain drain, popularly known as the “Japan syndrome.” He stated that the association acknowledged that the proposed bill reportedly contained safeguards for circumstances beyond practitioners’ control but insisted that such provisions must be explicit and enforceable. He called for the withdrawal and reconsideration of the proposed punitive provisions, alongside consultations involving healthcare associations, hospital administrators, patient representatives and other stakeholders. He urged the National Assembly to prioritise legislation guaranteeing adequate health funding, minimum emergency-care standards, appropriate staffing, constant electricity and functional referral systems. “We will consider all lawful options, including nationwide industrial action, if lawmakers proceeded with legislation unjustly criminalising doctors for institutional failures. “We however, pledged to make necessary arrangements to protect emergency and critically ill patients during any industrial action, while we reaffirm our commitment to patient safety and quality healthcare.,” he said. Gopax halted standard deposit and withdrawal services at 2:55 p.m. local time and stopped trading at 3:53 p.m., Yonhap News Agency reported , citing the exchange. Direct withdrawals through the website and app are unavailable. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are processed manually after internal verification. “To ensure the safe custody of user assets, we plan to transfer all virtual assets to cold wallets for storage,” Gopax said in remarks carried by Seoul Economic Daily. “Direct withdrawals through the Gopax website or app are temporarily unavailable, and customers wishing to withdraw funds should apply through the Gopax customer support center.” No actual loss of assets has been reported. Gopax said the shift of remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage is meant to shrink the surface available to anyone who can reach online systems. A Gopax official told Yonhap the email came from a party claiming it could hack the exchange, but that the threat itself had not been verified. “We ask for your understanding, as this measure is intended to prevent financial incidents and protect user assets,” the company said . entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. sports.description: Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since the Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago [Getty Images] It may be a surprise to some but Jobe Bellingham's call up to the England senior side has been a long time coming. Just like his older brother Jude - England's star player at the World Cup and one of Real Madrid's best players - Jobe's career path has been very similar. He too was a star of the Birmingham City academy before making a big-money move to the German Bundesliga and getting an England call-up. Jobe's debut for Birmingham came at the age of 16 years and 107 days. He was 69 days older than when Jude made his first appearance for the Blues' senior side. The centre midfielder then moved to Sunderland and helped them win promotion to the Premier League before joining German side Borussia Dortmund at the age of 19 in a deal worth up to £31m. Jude also moved to the German Club, when he was 17, before developing into one of the world's best players and joining Real Madrid. Having one of the best midfielders in the world as your older brother comes with challenges and Jobe has consistently been compared to his sibling. But the former Sunderland midfielder is his own player and wears 'Jobe' on the back of his shirt instead of his family name and said that it was suggested to him by a former coach because "it shows that I'm going my own way". Jobe is a different type of player to Jude, sitting deeper in the midfield but is as physically imposing while still being good on the ball. He is the current captain of the England U21 side and England manager Thomas Tuchel said the Young Lions head coach Lee Carsley had been pushing for some time for the younger Bellingham to get senior recognition. "He's the standout player. He's the captain, so the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time," said Tuchel. "That's what Jobe has done on top of it. He found his way, he found his rhythm with Dortmund. He's had an excellent start to his season, is a regular starter and influential." England host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before travelling to Madrid to take on Spain on 15 November in this next international break. With Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for the first game, and Bournemouth's Alex Scott out injured after shining on his debut in last month's 7-0 win over Croatia, Tuchel said that a natural "opportunity" for Jobe had opened up. sports.title: The breakdown battle that could decide England vs Australia
sports.description: It is about eight months since England’s men last trod the Twickenham turf, a long gap between hit-outs on home soil. That performance against Ireland will carry few happy memories for Steve Borthwick ’s squad – not that there is any conscious effort to right the wrongs. “If we’re going to sit and stew over a game eight months ago, we’re in f***** trouble,” a surprisingly spiky Richard Wigglesworth, the senior assistant coach, remarked this week. Still, England would be wise to reflect on their failings in that game. While there was plenty to learn from a lean Six Nations, it was that showing in the 42-21 defeat that most disappointed Borthwick and his selection, falling so far short of where they needed to be . It was at the breakdown where Ireland beasted them particularly, and in the two red zones especially: Andy Farrell’s side won 14 turnovers and limited England to just 1.3 points per 22 entry. England were heavily beaten by Ireland in the Six Nations (PA Wire) England’s difficulty at the breakdown was striking given their selection. That game remains Henry Pollock ’s only start at Test level; a back row of he, Tom Curry and Ben Earl should have provided plenty of ruck menace. But, perhaps, Borthwick was guilty of a redundancy of skillset. While Pollock and Earl are enterprising and prolific carriers, neither is a consistent resourcer of rucks; Curry, too, per Opta hit just 11.7 rucks per 80 minutes for Sale across the last Prem campaign, less than half that of Guy Pepper, a significant absentee for this campaign. That may be partly to do with Bath’s multi-phase preference, and also Curry’s usage as an edge forward in attack. Guy Pepper is a significant absentee (PA Wire) But against Ireland, England lacked big bodies in the tight exchanges, and found themselves bedevilled by Tadhg Beirne, Caelan Doris, Dan Sheehan and Josh van der Flier. It is notable that Borthwick, even with Pepper and Tom Curry injured, has not elected to pair Earl and Pollock again – the pair perhaps better dovetail in the second half, when the game loses some structure and each can use their athleticism to collect a volume of carries. Since his installation on the blindside for the France game in March, Ollie Chessum has provided better balance around the park and more variety at the lineout from which to launch. The inclusion of Ben Curry, who returns for a first England appearance since July 2025, provides the side with perhaps their best pure jackaller – even if his twin brother’s ability to steal time and bodies with ruck hustle will be missed. Ben Curry is set for his first England appearance since July 2025 (PA Wire) One of the challenges that Curry and the rest will face is stepping up from the Prem to Test level, where the brekadown is much more hotly contested. sports.description: Lambeth, shown winning the October 9 Sycamore Stakes at Keeneland, is the early favorite for Saturday's Grade III River City at Churchill Downs. Photo courtesy of Keeneland Oct. 6 (UPI) -- Tuesday's Melbourne Cup, inconveniently scheduled just three days after the Breeders' Cup, produced a trifecta win for trainer Ciaron Maher and for horses bred in the British Isles. Next up are the Japan Cup, with the Aga Khan's Studs' Calandagan hoping to double up on his historic victory a year ago, and then Hong Kong's iconic year-end international races with big names from around the world in the early-entry box. Back in North America, horse racing catches its breath after another successful return of the Breeders Cup to Keeneland. Around the world, around the clock Australia It's unusual to see a trainer saddle the first three finishers in any race, much less a top-level race (think Aidan O'Brien and Chad Brown). But how about "the race that stops the nation" -- the Melbourne Cup? That's the hat trick that Ciaron Maher pulled off Tuesday at Flemington. Point of Law went off favorite at 6-1 and showed that was value, winning by 3 3/4 lengths from 25-1 stablemate Zahrann. Juja Kibo completed the hat trick, just a nose farther behind. The closest rival was the Joseph O'Brien shipper Sons and Lovers, another 1 1/4 lengths in arrears. Maher had a strong hand with seven horses in the field of 23, also including Royal Supremacy, who shot away to a gigantic lead before handing over to his stablemate. The trainer became the first to score the Melbourne Cup trifecta. "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but we just had to execute," Maher said in post-race interview. "I certainly didn't know that Royal Supremacy would lead by that far, but it is a true test of staying and, Point of Law, he's just thrived. sports.title: Women's rights matter more than any league, say Afghan cricketers
sports.description: Firooza Amiri and Nahida Sapan were among the Afghan women's players to flee to Australia [Getty Images] Afghan women's cricketers have accused overseas players signing up for the inaugural Afghanistan Premier League of sending a message to the world that women suffering in the country "can simply be ignored". Women's participation in sport has been effectively outlawed since the Taliban's return to power in 2021, and many of Afghanistan's female cricketers left the country for their own safety. The men's franchise league is expected to start in December in the UAE, though it is yet to be sanctioned by the International Cricket Council (ICC). In September, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) urged players to reconsider their involvement and batter Ollie Pope withdrew. "For five years, girls in Afghanistan have been denied the right to play cricket and many other basic rights," Nahida Sapan, who captained the Afghanistan Refugee Women's XI on this summer's tour of England, told the BBC Stumped podcast . "Foreign players had a real opportunity to stand with millions of Afghan women and girls by choosing not to participate. "It may have seemed like a small action, but it could have sent a powerful message and put pressure on those responsible. "This is not about being against cricket or Afghan men's cricket. It is about standing up for basic human rights." Eight English players were signed in the draft on Tuesday, alongside players from Scotland, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand. England's Alex Hales, Tymal Mills, Joe Clarke, Olly Stone, Moeen Ali, Luke Wood, Tom Moores and Chris Wood were all signed. Scotland's George Munsey also secured a deal, as did Ireland all-rounder Curtis Campher. Other England players including Dawid Malan and James Vince also put their names into the draft. England will have more overseas representation than any other country in the Afghan league. The major names signed from other nations include Sri Lanka internationals Kusal Perera, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera and Kamindu Mendis, Australian batter D'Arcy Short, South Africa spinner Imran Tahir and Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan. The ECB has refused to schedule bilateral cricket with Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power - a stance Australia also adopts. England have, however, continued to play against Afghanistan at global events, including World Cups in both limited-overs formats and the Champions Trophy, which resulted in calls from MPs for their game in 2025 to be boycotted. "For me, the women and girls of Afghanistan come first," said Sapan. "Their rights, dignity and freedom matter more than any league or sporting opportunity. "Taking part in this league without acknowledging what is happening to Afghan women risks sending the message to the world that their suffering can simply be ignored." sports.description: Scott Pollock previously played for Brackley Town, where he made 70 appearances [Getty Images] Oxford City midfielder Scott Pollock believes there is "no reason" his side cannot pile more pressure on his beloved Leicester City by pulling off an FA Cup upset when they host the Foxes on Friday night. The National League North side welcome the former Premier League and FA Cup winners to The MGroup Stadium in the first round of this season's competition, under the lights on their artificial pitch. Pollock, who joined the non-leaguers in July, is relishing coming up against his boyhood club, who he supports and tried out for as a youngster. "It just felt like it was meant to be as a Leicester fan myself," he told BBC Radio Oxford. "Away (from home) would have been nice but I feel that at home we have a good chance of going through. From playing against Messi and Ronaldo to non-league Forestieri ready for fresh challenge at Oxford City Oxford City have made it to the first round proper for the first time in four years, having narrowly beaten Torquay United in the final qualifying round. Pollock, 25, has personal experience of an Oxford City shock. He was a Northampton Town player in 2020 when the part-time Hoops beat their League One opponents 2-1 in an FA Cup giant-killing. And he believes the pressure is all on the third-tier Foxes, who have struggled in their start to the League One campaign following back-to-back relegations from the Premier League and the Championship. "There's just a feeling of excitement among us really," Pollock added. "The pressure's on them to do well in the league and in the cup - we're at home and we know the pitch so it favours us in that aspect. "That being said, we know they're a good team so we have to be up for it. Oxford City have done cup upsets before and there is no reason why we can't do it again." From Youtube to playing on TV in the FA Cup Pollock has had a somewhat unique footballing journey, first making a name for himself on YouTube with Hashtag United. Spencer Owen co-founded Hashtag with his brother Seb Carmichael-Brown in 2016 and ran an academy series on their channel in 2017. Pollock ended up winning the series and then played for their first team, starring in a charity game called the Wembley Cup where he won man of the match and was rewarded with a trial at Premier League side Crystal Palace. A year later he moved to Northampton, where he made 29 senior appearances, scoring two goals. "They were trying to find the next star," he recalled of the Hashtag series, having applied for it when he was just 16. "I didn't think anything of it when I applied for it and I ended up winning it out of 20,000 people. "It was a good experience when I was younger and I got to play men's football from a young age so it's helped a lot in my career."

technology.title: Blue Origin unveils more thrust, less haste as New Glenn slips to 2027
technology.description: New Glenn's return to flight has slipped to January 2027, according to a leaked staff memo from Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp, overshadowing the company's announcements of a new third stage and booster engine. Blue Origin has been rebuilding after its New Glenn rocket exploded during a ground test in May , extensively damaging the launchpad. A month later, the company's CEO, Dave Limp, said that Blue Origin "still plan[s] to fly again this year," which raised a few eyebrows in the space and rocket community. The detonation had pretty much destroyed the facility, and getting back into the launch business so quickly seemed optimistic. That timetable has now slipped. In the memo circulating on social media, Limp praised the team's efforts but said: "We're proactively updating our anticipated launch date to January 2027." A small slip given the damage, but one that leaves less breathing room before NASA's planned Artemis III demonstration mission, involving lunar technologies from Blue Origin and SpaceX, next year. The delay emerged as the Bezos-backed company unveiled GS3, a third stage for New Glenn , designed for missions including direct injection into geostationary orbit and Earth-escape trajectories. The company said: "GS3 is already under contract for a cislunar mission with a government customer scheduled to launch in 2028." Blue Origin says the stage is not required for its lunar lander architecture, although it could support sustained operations around the Moon. The company also unveiled Northstar , a booster engine it says has half the parts and 30 percent less mass than its BE-4, while increasing thrust from 640,000 to 715,000 pounds-force. The memo said the team had "found and fixed the issue that caused the anomaly," without elaborating. Limp said in August that the problem "originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines" and that existing engines would need retrofitting, but did not explain how the valve failed or what changes were required. The Register asked Blue Origin for comment. ®

technology.title: TikTok’s For You page needs to change, says the EU
technology.description: The European Commission claims TikTok broke its online platform rules by offering a recommendation algorithm that creates a "rabbit hole effect" on users. In an announcement on Friday, the regulators allege TikTok's algorithm can harm users with "endless and repeated exposure" to content related to sadness, isolation, or body image. technology.title: DigiCert admits 16-month security lapse exposed customer information
technology.description: DigiCert has admitted that a botched server migration left an internal system exposed to the internet for more than a year, allowing an unauthorized user to access customer data, including passports, driver's licenses, and other identity documents. The certificate authority has begun notifying affected customers but has yet to disclose how many people had their information exposed. In an email seen by The Register , DigiCert confirmed the compromised information included names, business email addresses, phone numbers, and business addresses. Some records may also have contained passports, driver's licenses, utility bills, or other identification documents. "We are completing a review of identification documents to determine the specific individuals involved," DigiCert told those affected, adding that it would notify those people once the review was complete. DigiCert's incident report traces the blunder back to February 2025, when an internal business system was moved from a VPN-protected network to a different availability zone. That change also opened the system up to the public internet, where it sat for more than 16 months without DigiCert realizing. The archive used the same account management platform as DigiCert's customer-facing products, including a self-registration feature that was never supposed to be available on the internal system. This allowed outsiders to create accounts without multifactor authentication and, thanks to a separate permissions flaw, use them to browse archived customer records. DigiCert found the unauthorized accounts on June 18, 2026, but initially dismissed them as harmless because they weren't assigned to an application. A security researcher raised the alarm about the account creation issue three days later, but it took until July 2 for DigiCert to shut it down. Unfortunately, someone had already been poking around. It wasn't until October 12 that DigiCert began investigating whether customer information had actually been accessed. On October 19, it confirmed that an unauthorized account had accessed a subset of archived records between June 27 and July 2. DigiCert described the affected records as a "small proportion" of its archive but hasn't disclosed how many customers or individuals were caught up in the breach. The company did not respond to The Register ’s questions at the time of publication. DigiCert's postmortem makes for uncomfortable reading. The server move didn't get a proper security review, monitoring failed to pick up suspicious activity, and the access controls weren't much use against self-registered accounts. The company has since switched off self-registration, tightened network access, and added monitoring that might have come in handy a few months earlier. technology.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) looks set to win more than a billion pounds of UK taxpayers' money under a new Home Office contract for public cloud hosting. A planning notice , published on October 30, covers the renewal of the department's public cloud services, to meet its current and future hosting needs. The estimated value is £881,621,007 ($1.18 billion), which passes £1 billion once VAT is included. AWS won the existing contract with the Home Office in 2023 for about £450 million (c $603 million). The Register has asked the Home Office why the figure has risen so much, and will update this article if it responds. Once awarded, the contract is expected to run from December 2027 to December 2029, with a possible extension to December 2031 (four years in total). A market engagement event for suppliers on the G-Cloud 15 Lot 1A procurement framework is scheduled for December 8, giving bidders the chance to pitch. technology.title: Bank of England pours cold water on AI productivity boom
technology.description: Despite the billions being thrown at artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered little in the way of productivity gains for UK businesses, according to the Bank of England. In its latest Monetary Policy Report , the central bank found that AI has increased UK productivity by an estimated 0.5 percent over the past three years. That works out to just 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points of additional annual productivity growth since early 2024, hardly the economic revolution Silicon Valley has been promising. "AI investment appears to be contributing somewhat to current demand strength, but so far there is only evidence of a modest AI-driven rise in UK productivity growth," the Bank said. Even industries supposedly best placed to benefit from the technology have little to boast about. Productivity growth has improved in AI-heavy sectors such as information and communications, but has yet to exceed pre-pandemic averages. That's not to say AI isn't doing anything for the British economy. The bank estimates that AI-related activity has accounted for just under a fifth of UK GDP growth since the beginning of 2026, though much of that appears to come from companies developing and deploying the technology rather than businesses becoming more productive by using it. "The contribution to growth from AI to date appears to reflect activity in the upstream development and implementation of AI technologies rather than broader gains from their adoption elsewhere in the economy," the report said. In other words, selling AI is proving rather more lucrative than actually using it, The bank also cautioned against giving AI too much credit for Britain's recent productivity improvements. Much of the increase appears to reflect businesses hiring fewer workers while output continues to grow, partly as companies unwind post-pandemic staffing decisions and respond to higher employment costs. And despite predictions that AI will make vast swathes of the workforce redundant, firms responding to the Bank's Decision Maker Panel survey reported virtually no overall impact on employment so far. The technology is, however, making some employers less inclined to hire new staff or replace those who leave. Other studies suggest businesses are still waiting for the payoff. A Gartner survey published last month found that while three-quarters of corporate board members expected AI to improve productivity and cut costs, just 3 percent of organizations had actually achieved their targets. Meanwhile, 38 percent were already over budget on AI spending, yet 85 percent planned to spend even more next year. Another study involving nearly 6,000 executives , published in February, found that more than 80 percent of firms had seen no discernible impact from AI on either employment or productivity. An amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, which is passing through Parliament , would give ministers powers to regulate the deployment and reporting of agentic AI in certain organizations. The new clause was introduced during the bill's third reading in the House of Lords this week. In an explanatory note , ministers outlined plans for safeguards, notification of affected organizations, preservation of evidence, and government-led incident reviews. The measures would require consultation and parliamentary approval through secondary legislation. The move follows a series of incidents. Last month, OpenAI revealed that its agents repeatedly strayed beyond their intended scope , prompting the company to notify more than 100 organizations about the issues. That came after July's incident, in which an OpenAI agent accessed the internet and breached machine learning platform Hugging Face . The episode, and the potential for more damage from poorly designed AI agent deployments, have prompted MPs to question whether UK law can deal with such threats. Speaking to The Register , Stuart Davey, a partner at law firm Pinsent Masons, described the clause as "quite novel." Rather than directly imposing new duties, it would allow ministers to introduce rules and investigatory powers covering regulated organizations. Davey said that could include powers "to look where there has been such an AI agentic compromise or issue, and do some things... appoint inspectors, enter and search premises, seize and retain documents." Under the proposals, the minister could confer certain powers on regulators, requiring action from targeted organizations. Potentially affected organizations include gas and electricity suppliers, managed service providers, and cloud providers deploying AI agents for customers. Foundation model developers would not automatically fall within scope simply because they build the underlying technology. "Where there's a security or operational compromise in relation to a relevant network or information system, that would seem to capture those managed service providers or cloud computing providers who are using AI, and there's that loss of control," said Davey. He advised cloud and managed service providers to track whether the proposed measures become law. If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho. What is happening? The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun , a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space. Coronal holes appear darker in ultraviolet images because they are cooler and less dense than their surroundings. And this particularly large — and rather oddly shaped — coronal hole is sending some seriously speedy wind our way. The culprit is a large coronal hole in the sun, shaped a bit like a witch on a broom... The fast solar winds are expected to arrive around Nov. 6-7 and could persist through much of the weekend. It could interact with Earth's magnetic field , potentially triggering geomagnetic storms and fueling spectacular aurora shows. The stronger the storm, the farther south the northern lights can potentially be seen.
